meta.subtitle: Margins and cash flow are rising, but near the 52-week high the shares already price in most of it

analystCommentary:
Red Violet's second quarter of 2026 improved on the year-ago quarter across the lines the MD&A reports: revenue, gross margin, net income and operating cash flow all rose. The business has grown revenue at double-digit rates in each of the last four fiscal years.

The share price has moved to reflect that. At $79.55 on October 2, 2026 the stock sits close to its 52-week high of $81.80, against a low of $33.40. It trades at 70.4x trailing earnings, and the consensus target of $84.50 implies only +6.2% from here.

The August 2026 equity offering adds a second question to the operating one: what the company does with the new cash (see Management).

We rate RDVT HOLD with a $72–$90 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Red Violet, Inc. is an analytics and information solutions company that delivers identity intelligence in the United States. Its cloud-native platform, CORE, combines public records, proprietary and publicly-available data with machine learning to identify and locate people, businesses, assets and their relationships.

The company markets its solutions mainly through two brands. IDI's flagship product, idiCORE, is an investigative tool used for due diligence, identity authentication, fraud prevention, regulatory compliance and debt recovery by financial services firms, insurers, law enforcement, law firms, collections agencies and others. FOREWARN is an app-based solution that gives professionals information about a consumer before a face-to-face meeting.

Red Violet reports a single segment, earns substantially all of its revenue from licensing its solutions, and is headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida.

thesis.body: The business case is good: double-digit growth, widening margins and strong cash conversion. The valuation case is weaker. At the current price the shares already discount most of the outcome we think likely, so our probability-weighted fair value sits close to the current price (see Valuation). We hold the stock rather than buy it.

catalysts: How management deploys the proceeds of the August 2026 equity offering, including any acquisition.
Third-quarter 2026 results and whether the second-quarter margin gains hold.
Continued customer and user growth at IDI and FOREWARN.
Use of the remaining authorization under the Stock Repurchase Program.
risks: A valuation that leaves little room for a slowdown.
A data breach or privacy incident at a company that stores sensitive consumer information.
An acquisition that overpays or proves hard to integrate.
Dilution from the August 2026 share issue.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $90.3M, up {+20.0%+}, after growth of 24.9% in FY24 and 12.9% in FY23. Operating margin has risen every year in the series, from -3.0% in FY21 to 14.6% in FY25. FY25 net income was $13.2M, or $0.91 per diluted share.

The second quarter of 2026 extended the trend. Revenue rose 23% to $26.7 million, gross margin increased to 76% from 72%, and net income rose 85% to $5.0 million, or $0.34 per diluted share. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 million, a 42% margin against 35% a year earlier.

The counter-case is the gap between adjusted and reported profit. Adjusted EBITDA excludes share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, while the trailing operating margin is 17.9% and the trailing net margin 16.5%. The 70.4x trailing P/E rests on that GAAP profit, so the stock is more expensive than the adjusted margin makes it look.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and cash equivalents were $50.0 million at June 30, 2026, and the trailing current ratio is 10.88. Our data reports no debt for FY22 to FY25; that is a gap in the data rather than a confirmed zero, but nothing in the filing excerpt points to borrowing.

The August 2026 offering of 1,916,667 shares brought net proceeds of approximately $109.0 million. That arrived after the quarter end, so it is not in the June balance. The issue is more than a tenth of the ~16.05M shares outstanding. That share count is derived from the October 2, 2026 market cap, so it likely already includes the new shares. Per-share growth now has to absorb the larger share base.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $28.8M in FY25, a 31.9% FCF margin against 19.7% in FY21. Purchases of property and equipment were small at -$563,000 in FY25. The company's own FCF definition also deducts capitalized costs included in intangible assets, which our data does not break out. Second-quarter 2026 net cash provided by operating activities rose to $10.6 million.

The business funds itself comfortably. The issue is price: at the current market value the trailing FCF yield is 2.6%, which gives a holder little cash return while waiting for growth to compound.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $79.55 RDVT trades at 70.4x trailing earnings, 47.9x NTM earnings, 12.9x trailing sales and 66.0x trailing EV/EBITDA. The snapshot's forward P/E on FY27E is ~45.2x; we use the NTM figure as the main forward measure.

Consensus EPS is $1.66 for FY26E and $1.76 for FY27E, against FY25 diluted EPS of $0.91. The step from FY25 to FY26E may reflect a different basis rather than growth alone: in the second quarter the company reported GAAP diluted EPS of $0.34 and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50, and the consensus basis is not stated. Our valuation uses the GAAP-based trailing and NTM multiples. From FY26E to FY27E, consensus EPS grows much more slowly than revenue, which runs from $106.7M to $120.8M; the new shares from the August offering are one factor weighing on that per-share path.

The Street is uniformly positive but sees limited upside: all 4 covering analysts rate Buy, with a consensus target of $84.50, a median of $87.50 and a range of $73.00–$90.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against, so we judge the price against the growth rate and the cash yield instead.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue growth holds near recent rates, margins keep widening, and the offering proceeds fund an acquisition the market sees as accretive. The shares rise above the top of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The company delivers consensus revenue and earnings, the cash is deployed slowly, and the multiple holds roughly where it is. The shares end near the Street consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The slower FY27E per-share earnings path in consensus becomes the market's focus. Investors re-rate RDVT as a slower-growing business and the multiple contracts, taking the shares below the bottom of the Street target range while staying above the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only consensus delivery at an unchanged multiple. Bear gets more weight than Bull because its trigger is already visible in consensus: the earnings path flattens from FY26E to FY27E on a larger share count. Bull, by contrast, depends on an acquisition that has not been identified.

The gap between the Bull and Bear prices reflects the starting multiple: from today's trailing multiple, a re-rating down moves the price more than continued delivery moves it up.

The result is a weighted fair value of $78.40, an expected upside of -1.4% and a bear-case downside of -30.9%. That falls short of our BUY threshold, and the downside is larger than the expected return.

Our $72–$90 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Red Violet reports a single segment and does not break out revenue by brand. The MD&A gives operating measures instead: as of June 30, 2026 IDI had 10,869 billable customers against 9,549 a year earlier, and FOREWARN had 443,173 users against 346,671. In the three months ended June 30, 2026, 77% of revenue was attributable to customers with pricing contracts, which are generally annual or longer with auto renewal, and 23% to transactional customers. That gives good visibility, although contract customers can still pay partly on usage, so not all of that contracted share is fixed.

moatFactors.name: Data assets and platform
moatFactors.body: CORE combines several data sources with machine learning built into the platform. In our view, maintaining such datasets and the analytics on top of them takes sustained investment. The 10-K warns that the data and analytics sector changes rapidly, so this advantage lasts only as long as that investment continues.

moatFactors.name: Workflow embedding
moatFactors.body: The company's land-and-expand model starts with a trial and grows as customers add use cases across departments and become reliant on the solutions in their daily workflow. The rise in IDI billable customers and the contract structure (see Segments) are consistent with that. Customers can still move to another data provider at renewal.

moatFactors.name: FOREWARN distribution
moatFactors.body: 660 REALTOR Associations are now contracted to use FOREWARN, which gives the product an established channel to its users. In our view, that network is an advantage a new entrant would need time to match. The same channel ties FOREWARN to a single industry, since the MD&A describes it as currently tailored for real estate.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Rising margins and contracted, renewing revenue are consistent with real customer reliance. We stop short of wide because the company is small, its data advantage depends on continued investment, and a single serious security incident could undo customer trust quickly. The moat holds if CORE keeps pace with technology change and the company avoids a breach.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$106.7M, up 18%, a slight slowdown from FY25. That is a reasonable bar given the second-quarter pace, but it is the bar the current price already assumes.
In the second quarter, IDI added 447 customers and FOREWARN added 25,493 users. The year-on-year rise in both counts (see Segments) supports the land-and-expand model described in Moat.
Acquisitions are the new swing factor. A well-priced deal funded from the offering could add growth that the organic numbers do not yet show (see Management).
In our view, FOREWARN's reach beyond real estate (see Moat) is an open question; any broadening would be new growth the numbers do not yet show.

management.leadership: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we do not name or comment on individual executives. The MD&A describes the operating approach: an inside sales team, a strategic sales team for major accounts, and distributors, resellers and strategic partners, with management continuing to build out the sales organization. The steady rise in operating margin over five years (see Financials) is the main evidence of execution available to us.
management.capitalAllocation:
Red Violet pays no dividend. Year to date through June 30, 2026 it purchased 74,500 shares at an average price of $41.87 under its Stock Repurchase Program, with $15.5 million remaining on the authorization. In August 2026 it then issued 1,916,667 new shares. On net, the share count rose: holders took dilution in exchange for roughly $109.0 million of cash.

That trade pays off only if the cash earns more than it costs in dilution. Management intends to use the proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes, including potential strategic acquisitions, and names no target. Cash held on the balance sheet earns little, so the measure to watch is what any acquisition costs relative to the revenue and cash flow it adds.
management.governance: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we cannot assess board composition and independence, executive pay, insider ownership or related-party dealings. We make no governance claims beyond that gap, and readers should consult the company's latest proxy before relying on this section.

idiosyncratic: Data security: the 10-K says the company aggregates, stores and processes a large amount of sensitive consumer information, and that a breach could cause a material loss of business, legal liability or reputational harm. It also notes that insurance may not cover the full cost.

Privacy: the 10-K warns that privacy concerns or an unauthorized disclosure of personal information could harm the company's reputation, cost it customers, or bring claims or litigation, and that complying with state and federal privacy and breach-notification laws carries significant costs.
Technology change: the 10-K says success depends on developing new products in a timely manner and that competitors' products could make existing ones obsolete.
Capital deployment: in our view, the offering proceeds raise the risk of an overpriced or poorly integrated acquisition (see Management).
Valuation: the multiple-compression path set out in the Bear scenario.
risks.systemic: In our view, demand from the customer groups the MD&A lists, including financial services, insurance, collections and real estate professionals, could weaken if activity in those industries slows. A change in federal or state privacy law could also affect the whole identity-data industry at once; that is our view, not a risk the 10-K excerpt frames as regulatory change. As a small-cap growth stock, RDVT is also exposed to shifts in market appetite for growth equities.

body: HOLD, target range $72–$90, on the scenario math in Valuation.

We would move to BUY on a share price near the bottom of our target range with the business still on the consensus path, or on an acquisition at a price that adds to per-share earnings. We would turn more cautious if revenue growth slows well below consensus or if a security incident occurs.
